# Lance format fixtures

The original datasets were generated by official Lance. The input to
`fsl_f64_nonnull.lance` had a non-nullable Float64 child. Official Lance
omits that child contract. Its read schema has a nullable child.

`fsl_f64_child_nonnull.lance` was generated by the in-house writer for #147.
It contains 50 rows of eight Float64 values. Flattened value `i` is
`i * 0.125`. Both the `vector` field and its `item` child are non-nullable.
The tests check the schema and values against independently built inputs.

To regenerate the in-house fixture, choose a new output directory:

```sh
cargo run --release --example generate_fsl_fixture -- /path/to/new-fixture.lance
```

The writer creates random artifact names. Compare decoded values and schemas,
not file names or dataset bytes.

## Child nullability metadata

Primitive fixed-size lists use one Lance leaf field and one physical column.
The in-house writer stores `genegraph-storage:fsl-child-nullable` in that
protobuf field's metadata. Its value is the UTF-8 text `true` or `false`.
The manifest and data-file schema carry the same value.

The reader uses this value for the Arrow child field and decoded array.
It removes the internal stamp from the returned Arrow schema. A missing
stamp retains the official nullable default. Invalid values and stamps on
scalar fields produce `StorageError::Invalid`. Callers cannot supply this
reserved field metadata key.

This is an in-house schema extension in the existing protobuf metadata map.
Official readers do not interpret it and can still return a nullable child.
Old files cannot recover child nullability that was not stored.
